title: engram.admission-assessment.v1 decision envelope
description: The exact, deterministic object whose RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical UTF-8 bytes are SHA-256 hashed to produce decision_hash. A verifier in any runtime that can canonicalize per RFC 8785 reproduces the same sha256:<hex>. Invocation identity (assessment id, evaluation/job/request ids, actor principal, created_at/evaluated_at) and all mutable projection state are deliberately absent: the hash identifies a decision over inputs and policy, not one execution of it. A matching hash proves what was decided, from which inputs, under which policy version. It proves nothing about factual truth or external endorsement.

mode.description: A shadow preview, an authoritative evaluation and a legacy import are different claims about the same state, so the mode is part of what is hashed.

input_digest.description: SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 bytes of the item/governance/evidence state actually EVALUATED — strictly pre-mutation. On an admission this binds review_status='proposed', because that is the state policy read and authorized the transition out of; hashing post-mutation state here would make the record assert that policy admitted an already-active item. Excludes #157 evidence-assessment identity, which is diagnostic in v1 and must not behave like a promotion input.

resulting_state_digest.description: SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 bytes of the state this decision's own authorized mutation was expected to PRODUCE, or null when the decision changed nothing. Freshness resolves against this when present, so a decision is never stale by virtue of its own effect — an admission stays current immediately after it commits, and a promotion-time conflict block stays current after writing the conflict metadata its recheck caused. A later unrelated change still makes the decision stale normally. Only a non-shadow decision whose outcome is admitted or blocked may carry one.

policy_profile_key.description: v1 defines exactly one production profile: the current two-lane Path A behavior.

policy_config_digest.description: SHA-256 over the RFC 8785 bytes of every decision-affecting configuration value and policy constant, plus the evaluated item's kind auto-promotion eligibility fact. Contains no timestamps, job ids, request ids, or other volatile invocation metadata.

selected_basis.description: The trust lane current policy selected, or null when no lane qualified.

outcome.description: Precedence when several categories apply: stale > blocked > review_required > cooling > insufficient_evidence > unknown, except that a successful mutation is always admitted and its non-mutating shadow equivalent is always would_admit. unknown is never coerced into insufficient_evidence or a zero score.

blocker_codes.description: The canonical promotion blocker vocabulary, de-duplicated and sorted. Sorting is required: the evaluator emits blockers in discovery order, which depends on which lane it examined first, so an unsorted list would hash the same decision two different ways.

reason_codes.description: Closed explanation vocabulary, sorted. Versioned with the schema: adding a code is an ADR/schema change.

decision_inputs.description: Only safe normalized values current Path A actually read, including both lanes' trust and age qualification — which is what lets cooling be proven rather than inferred from an age blocker alone. Never memory content, transcript text, extraction spans, provider output, credentials, unrestricted conflict candidates, or human-evaluation labels.

conflict_recheck_status.description: not_run_preview is the exact v1 value for a shadow/preview evaluation, which never runs the promotion-time semantic recheck. unavailable_legacy marks a legacy import where no recheck fact was ever recorded — an honest gap, never a clear result.

next_evaluation_at.description: Required whenever next_actions contains wait_until; null when no deterministic due time exists, rather than an invented schedule.

next_actions.description: Bounded set in fixed order, so the hash does not depend on discovery order. Multiple actions appear when independently required.
